gen-dafont-origami-gf-khula: Contemporary and a bit unusual, Origami draws brush-style letters at constant width, with a lowercase as dense as poured lead. Khula follows with a tall midsection and curves that keep their mouths open, so a size bump for the body would be unnecessary.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-krub: Krub reads modern and level-headed, with a pronounced x-height and curves that stop before the loop closes. Origami's brush-drawn heading gives it a bold, solid partner.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-kufam: Kufam draws every line like a neon sign tube, its curves in the e generously open. Make Origami small and its heavy brush-painted lowercase loses its punch, while a large Kufam would swallow the line, since its bodies dominate and the ascenders hardly show.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-lexend: Lexend reads approachable, with outsized lowercase and open jaws on every curve, and its thickness never shifts around a bend. Against Origami's dense brush lettering, that openness is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-lexend-deca: Lexend Deca draws a plain, unshaded line that never swells. Its terminals stop short of curling inward and its capitals look small beside big lowercase, so a long passage feels smooth and unhurried under Origami's single-stroke brush heading.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-liter: Liter reads modern, with no stroke contrast whatsoever. Its lowercase stands tall and its round forms have wide mouths, so enlarging the body a notch lets that vertical presence stand up to Origami's brush-painted weight.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-mada: Origami holds a ruler-straight line weight in a brush-sign style. Mada, a sans-serif with a towering midzone and curves that refuse to close, makes a longer passage feel approachable and easy to move through.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-martel-sans: Martel Sans reads neutral and modern, with generous openings in every curve and a high mean line across each word. Shrink Origami and its thick brush curves lose their ring, since they match a straight stem in weight while the body stays light.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-matangi: Matangi presses strokes like twine into a flat surface, leaving its rounded letters open and its lowercase hefty. And beside Origami's single-stroke brush heading, a longer passage reads as sturdy and unhurried, both fonts contemporary in feel.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-maven-pro: Maven Pro reads modern and unfussy, with a welcoming gap in the c, a gentle monotone line and a high-waisted lowercase. Origami's brush heading gives it contrast.
